A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Tool-Planner and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–H. The changed title and layout do not prevent reliable matching of their content.

before.justification: v1 reports original ToolBench experiments, clustering ablations, latency measurements and smaller-model experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original APIBench evaluations across three API platforms in Table 2.

M1.justification: Both retain SimCSE embeddings, k-means++ clustering, toolkit-based planning, within-toolkit substitution and cross-toolkit replanning. Algorithm 1 and Appendix G prompts preserve the procedure; the equation-index discrepancies do not establish an actual algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds APIBench evaluation using TorchHub, HuggingFace and TensorFlow model APIs alongside the retained ToolBench tasks. This substantially broadens evaluation from RapidAPI services to model-library API selection and invocation.

E2.justification: The evaluated baselines remain ReACT, Reflexion, AdaPlanner and DFSDT, including their extension to APIBench. Clustering and smaller-model comparator sets are also retained. Toolchain* appears in v2's qualitative feature matrix, without an added performance evaluation.

E3.justification: The new APIBench evaluation introduces hallucination rate and uses k=65 clusters. ToolBench retains k=1800, its existing test groups, model versions and inference temperature. The PDFs do not document a revision to the retained experiments' protocols.

E4.justification: Toolkit-integration ablations, cluster-count sensitivity, embedding comparisons, latency analysis, error examples, smaller-model analysis and case studies are retained. v2 Figure 5 redisplays the error distribution from v1 Table 4; the new benchmark's hallucination metric does not constitute a separate robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new APIBench table continues the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 adds APIBench pass, win and hallucination results across three platforms and three language models. For example, GPT-4 Tool-Planner averages are reported as 76.9%, 82.2% and 9.4%, respectively. Existing ToolBench, ablation, latency, error-distribution and Appendix D numerical results are retained.

T1.justification: The displayed state definitions change: Section 2 now includes xi among its own conditioning inputs, and Equation 2 excludes the current tool output that v1 included. These appear to be indexing inconsistencies rather than theoretical advances. The clustering objective and appendix search-complexity discussion remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about toolkit-based planning, thorough exploration and improved success and efficiency. The introduction adds APIBench results as supporting evidence without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation attributing reduced APIBench hallucinations to repeated attempts, failed-plan rejection and selection of callable APIs. It removes v1's dedicated single-tool interpretation. Appendix A retains the same limitations concerning clustering quality and latency.

D1.justification: v2 documents APIBench's 1,645-API setup and k=65 clustering configuration. Existing model identifiers, temperature, embedding implementation, prompts and reported code access remain unchanged. Appendix B supplies no corresponding expansion of APIBench-specific sampling or scoring instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds Patil et al.'s Gorilla reference for APIBench and a feature matrix positioning Tool-Planner against existing planning frameworks. The main related-work discussion and other distinct cited works are retained; consolidating duplicate Reflexion references does not remove a research comparator.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and author information, converts citations to author-year style, locally rewrites methodology passages and renames the exploration phases. It reorganizes benchmark discussion and swaps the embedding and efficiency analyses, while retaining most prose and appendix content.

P2.justification: v2 adds feature-comparison and APIBench tables, reorganizes the toolkit ablation table into with/without blocks, highlights Tool-Planner result rows and replaces the error table with a pie chart. It also adopts the ICLR layout and relocates appendix floats. Figures 1–4 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: APIBench adds useful evidence of applicability to model-library APIs beyond v1's ToolBench evaluation. The gain is limited by sparse benchmark-specific protocol details and new reporting errors. In v2 Table 2, GPT-4 DFSDT's platform win scores average 69.7%, rather than the reported 67.7%; ordinary averaging therefore supports a 12.5-point advantage instead of the advertised 14.5 points. New equation-index inconsistencies also weaken precision, while the established experiments and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
